## Teaching points

1. Aortic dissection can present with neurological deficits and little or no pain; consider it in any acute non-traumatic paraplegia.
2. Anterior spinal artery syndrome: paraplegia, areflexia and loss of pain and temperature sensation with preserved vibration and proprioception.
3. Symmetric pulses and limb pressures do not exclude dissection (pulse deficits are present in only a minority).
4. New lactic acidosis or rising creatinine in a 'neurological' patient suggests malperfusion; image the whole aorta.
5. Type A dissection needs emergency surgery; meanwhile beta-blockade first, then vasodilators, to cut aortic wall stress.
